Enumerate all four-element subsets of the seven old vertices, solve their supporting hyperplane equations over \(\mathbb Q\), and retain exactly the hyperplanes on whose nonnegative side all seven vertices lie. The same enumeration works for each middle polytope using its four facet vertices and the seven points \((V_i+a_4)/2\). Every facet contains four affinely independent extreme vertices, each among these eleven generators, so this enumeration produces the complete halfspace description, not a relaxation.

Use the unimodular linear chart \(w\mapsto Uw\), where

\[
U=\begin{pmatrix}
0&0&0&1\\

U^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}

\((0,0,0,0),(0,0,1,-5),(0,-3,-2,0),(0,-3,3,1),(1,2,2,-4),(1,-1,4,2),(2,-1,-3,2)\).
Thus \(UP_4\) lies in the integer box

Because \(a_4\in P_4\), convexity gives \((P_4+a_4)/2\subseteq P_4\), and consequently every middle polytope is contained in \(P_4\). The displayed old and middle censuses also specify every one of the 32 next parity classes: for \(b\in\{0,1\}^4\),
\(|(D_5)_{(b,0)}|=|(D_4)_b|+\mathbf1_{b\equiv a_4\pmod2}\) and
\(|(D_5)_{(b,1)}|=|(D_{4,1})_b|\).
In particular, each next support has exactly \(e\) empty classes, \(1+\sigma\) singleton classes, and no class of size at least four. This accounts for the top point at even new height; it does not incorrectly put it into an additional odd-height parity class.

For reflection, the containment \(D_{4,1}\subseteq D_4\) immediately gives \(r_{D_{4,1}}(j)\le r_{D_4}(j)\le3\) at every integer center. Enumerating unordered distinct same-parity pairs in each displayed middle census gives its displayed count-one labels. The exact certificate below checks every pair. The all-center formulas of 1abd4035daee7fe2 now read

\[
r_{D_5}((j,0))=r_{D_4}(j),\qquad
r_{D_5}((j,1))=r_{D_{4,1}}(j)+2\mathbf1_{\{a_4\}}(j),\qquad
r_{D_5}((j,2))=\mathbf1_{\{a_4\}}(j).
\]

All other integer heights have count zero. In the two \(f=4\) cases the pairs \((z_{20},z_{24})\) and \((z_{26},z_{29})\), respectively, have centers \(z_{21}\) and \(z_{27}\) and both endpoints belong to the corresponding middle census. Thus the cross center has middle count three and lifted count five. In every other row it has middle count one and lifted count three. The old bottom layer already has maximum three. This proves every reflection-maximum entry, including centers outside the support, where the complete lattice census and convexity force count zero.

If \(T\) denotes the count-one label list in a row, the full next count-one set is exactly
\(\{(z_i,0):i\in\{0,1,2,19,22,25,26,35,36\}\}\cup\{(z_i,1):i\in T\setminus\{\alpha\}\}\cup\{(a_4,2)\}\).
For \(f=4\) the only next center with count five is \((a_4,1)\). Every other next supported center outside this count-one set has count three. Thus the packet supplies all-center hereditary data, not just a cardinality.

For the facet assertion, write the old supporting inequality as \(H_f(w)=b+c\cdot w\ge0\), and put \(d=H_f(a_4)>0\). The inequality \(H_f(w)+d(1-u)\ge0\) holds on every generator of the next lift, where \(u\) is its new height. It is strictly positive on all bottom generators, zero on \((F_4^{(f)},1)\), and zero at \((a_4,2)\). Its equality face is exactly the asserted five-vertex simplex. Hence all four middle facet vertices survive, the old seven bottom vertices remain, and the top is a vertex. These are all possible vertices of the generating hull, so \(k_4=4\) and \(v_5=12\). The exact three integer layers give \(N_5=38+|D_{4,1}|\) and \(\delta_5=46-|D_{4,1}|\), which verify the scalar table.

For completeness, rederive the loss formula rather than assuming an additional defect packet. For any complete middle census \(E\) with maximum reflection count at most three, let \(s_b\) be all sixteen ambient parity sizes and \(t\) its number of count-one points. Ordered same-parity endpoint pairs are in bijection with oriented reflected pairs at integer centers, and every such center belongs to \(E\). Thus \(\sum_b s_b^2=3|E|-2t\). Subtracting \(5\sum_b s_b-6\cdot16\) yields

\[
2(48-|E|-t)=\sum_b(s_b-2)(s_b-3).
\]

Here \(E\subseteq D_4\), whose parity sizes are at most three. Each empty class contributes six on the right and each singleton contributes two, with sizes two and three contributing zero. Therefore \(q_{\mathrm{middle}}=3e+\sigma\). Since \(h=t-5\), direct substitution gives
\(q_{\mathrm{middle}}+h=43-|E|\) and
\(\delta_5=\delta_4+q_{\mathrm{middle}}+t-4-2=3+q_{\mathrm{middle}}+h\).
These identities remain valid in the two \(f=4\) rows because the middle maximum is still at most three; no false assumption about their lifted maximum is used.

For any apex in the old polytope, the same convex containment gives \(|E|\le37\), and hence \(q_{\mathrm{middle}}+h\ge6\). The desired no-empty condition and \(\sigma\le2\) would give \(q_{\mathrm{middle}}\le2\), while \(h\le2\) would give \(q_{\mathrm{middle}}+h\le4\), a contradiction. Equivalently, those bounds require \(|E|\ge39\), beyond the entire old census. This is a geometric obstruction to using an old singleton site itself as the apex; it is not a failure of the strict-side facet recurrence.

This inner family is genuinely disjoint from facet-vertex reflected apices. If \(P_4\subseteq\{\ell\le c\}\), \(v\in F_4=\{\ell=c\}\), and \(x\in P_4\), then \(\ell(2v-x)=2c-\ell(x)\ge c\). By contrast, the tested \(a_4=x\) satisfies \(\ell(a_4)<c\). Consequently the outside-or-on-facet observation about reflected anchors does not exclude or subsume this inner test.

The following deterministic certificate repeats all input coordinates, derives all supporting planes over \(\mathbb Q\), enumerates every integer point of the common 1152-point chart box, verifies the full middle and count-one censuses, checks the scalar table, and checks the actual next simplex facet. Its supporting-plane routine is the exhaustive rational hyperplane argument given above. Sage's \(\mathbb Q\)-polyhedra provide a separate exact representation check, not a floating-point feasibility test.

from itertools import combinations, product

     (8,14,20),(9,15,22),(10,17,25),(13,22,32),(14,24,35),

def primitive(row):
    row = vector(QQ,row)
    row *= lcm(t.denominator() for t in row)
    row /= gcd(ZZ(t) for t in row)
    return tuple(ZZ(t) for t in row)

def facets(vertices):
    result = {}
    for ix in combinations(range(len(vertices)),4):
        B = matrix(QQ,[(1,)+tuple(vertices[i]) for i in ix])
        if B.rank() != 4:
            continue
        row = primitive(B.right_kernel().basis()[0])
        values = [row[0]+sum(row[k+1]*v[k] for k in range(4))
                  for v in vertices]
        if min(values) < 0 < max(values):
            continue
        if max(values) <= 0:
            row = tuple(-t for t in row)
            values = [-t for t in values]
        result[row] = tuple(i for i,t in enumerate(values) if t == 0)
    return dict(sorted(result.items()))

H = [(0,0,0,0,1),(0,0,0,2,25),(0,0,5,-3,0),

     (0,156,0,-62,5),(155,-155,-108,133,0),
     (156,-156,-156,166,47)]

assert set(H) == {primitive(h.vector()) for h in P4.inequality_generator()}
assert [f for f,ix in enumerate(faces) if len(ix)==4] == [0,1,2,4,5,6,8]
box = list(product(range(3),range(-3,3),range(-3,5),range(-5,3)))
assert len(box) == 1152
assert all(0<=t[0]<=2 and -3<=t[1]<=2 and -3<=t[2]<=4
           and -5<=t[3]<=2 for t in [U*vector(ZZ,v) for v in V])

def census(rows):
    transformed = [(row[0],vector(QQ,row[1:])*Ui) for row in rows]
    return {tuple(ZZ(x) for x in Ui*vector(ZZ,t)) for t in box
            if all(b+sum(c[k]*t[k] for k in range(4))>=0
                   for b,c in transformed)}

parity = lambda x: tuple(t%2 for t in x)
parities = list(product(range(2),repeat=4))
def counts(E):
    return {j:sum(tuple(2*j[k]-x[k] for k in range(4)) in E
                  for x in E) for j in E}

assert census(H) == set(Z)
old_parity = [[i for i,z in enumerate(Z) if parity(z)==b] for b in parities]
assert old_parity == [[0,12,18],[27],[6,16],[21],[2,5,8],[23,31],

                     [30,34],[9,13,19],[26,29,35],[3,7],[20,24]]
old_counts = counts(set(Z))
assert max(old_counts.values()) == 3
assert sorted(Z.index(j) for j,r in old_counts.items() if r==1) == \
       [0,1,2,19,22,25,26,35,36]
assert old_counts[Z[21]] == old_counts[Z[27]] == 3

# Each row: alpha, f, middle labels, count-one labels,
# (N_middle,e,sigma,t,q_middle,h,r_m,r_a,r_5,N5,delta5).
cases = [

  [0,19,20,21,23,26,27,35,36],(12,7,6,9,27,4,3,1,3,50,34)),

  (9,7,9,9,30,4,1,1,3,47,37)),

 (27,0,list(range(22))+[26,27],[0,1,2,19,20,21,26,27],
  (24,4,4,8,16,3,3,1,3,62,22)),

  (8,8,8,8,32,3,1,1,3,46,38)),
 (27,2,[0,1,20,21,22,26,27,36],[0,1,20,21,22,26,27,36],
  (8,8,8,8,32,3,1,1,3,46,38)),
 (27,4,[0,20,21,22,24,25,26,27,29,30,31,32,33,34,35,36],
  [0,20,22,25,26,31,35,36],(16,6,6,8,24,3,3,3,5,54,30)),
 (27,5,[0,19,20,21,23,26,27,28,31,33,35,36],

  [0,2,19,20,21,23,26,27,28,36],(10,6,10,10,28,5,1,1,3,48,36)),

  (8,8,8,8,32,3,1,1,3,46,38))]

for alpha,f,I,T,expected in cases:
    a = Z[alpha]
    assert all(row[0]+sum(row[k+1]*a[k] for k in range(4))>0 for row in H)
    assert [z for z in Z if parity(z)==parity(a)] == [a]
    vertices = [V[i] for i in faces[f]] + \

    rows = facets(vertices)
    middle_poly = Polyhedron(vertices=vertices,base_ring=QQ)
    assert middle_poly.dim() == 4

    E = census(rows)

There is no random input, numerical rounding, or floating-point infeasibility inference. The stated family obstruction also has the independent convex-containment proof above.

For canonical Hellinger bookkeeping, use exactly the notation of 768d9712b73c4ab7: \(G=\ln(2^nH_*/W)\), where \(H_*=\max_jH_j\), and \(\rho=2^nM/W\). For the indicator table of a displayed next support, \(W=N_5\), \(M=1\), \(H_j=r_{D_5}(j)\), and therefore \(G=\ln(32\max_jr_{D_5}(j)/N_5)\) and \(\rho=32/N_5\). The convex-polytope indicator extends the table and preserves every zero lattice value. No moment quantity is called \(G\). In fact all these next supports have \(N_5\le62<64\), so they do not even meet the strict cardinality hypothesis \(|B|>2^{n+1}\) of the separation assertion discussed in 768d9712b73c4ab7. They supply neither a target disproof nor an infinite small-gain family.

One bounded next test is to move the unique cross midpoint by one unit in the above unimodular chart. Enumerate only
\(a_4=z_\alpha+2\varepsilon U^{-1}e_i\), with \(\alpha\in\{21,27\}\), \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), and \(i\in\{1,2,3,4\}\), where \(e_i\) are the four standard coordinate vectors. There are sixteen specified apices, before filtering.
